history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas — legend says Sati's right foot fell here; the shrine stands on a tortoise-hump-shaped hillock (Kurmaprshthakriti), hence Kurma Pitha. Built in 1501 CE by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in the Bengali Ek-ratna style, with the sacred Kalyan Sagar lake behind the temple. The state of Tripura is named after this temple. CSV town corrected: this temple is at Matabari/Udaipur (Gomati district), NOT Sabroom (~110 km away) — town field corrected. Opening-hours sources conflict (4 AM–10 PM vs 5 AM–9 PM vs 6 AM–9 PM) — verify before visit.

name: Tripura Sundari Temple
town_description: Udaipur is the ancient capital of the Manikya kings of Tripura, about 55 km south of Agartala in Gomati district. A town of temples, tanks and royal ruins, it is best known for the Tripura Sundari (Matabari) Shakti Peetha and the Gunabati group of temples.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~55-70 km)
travel.railway: Matabari railway station (~2 km) / Agartala (~55 km)
travel.road: On the Agartala–Udaipur road (NH-8); ~1.5–2 hours by road from Agartala

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Diwali brings the famous two-day mela and the largest crowds
